tier1.text: The medial rectus moves the eye toward the nose. The medial rectus is one of six extraocular muscles, the muscles that move the eye. Medial means toward the middle, and this muscle attaches to the side of the eyeball nearest the nose. To look at something close to the face, both medial rectus muscles turn the eyes toward the nose.

quotes.quote: As visual stimuli move closer to the face, the two medial recti muscles cause the eyes to move in the one nonconjugate movement that is part of gaze control. When the two eyes move to look at something closer to the face, they both adduct, which is referred to as convergence.
